memory: I established neoprene damping vs thickness and corrected τ0 artefact: preload altered τ0 only via contact geometry and dynamic compression. An aluminium shim control removed the τ0 shift. Today I built a 3.0 mm stainless annular shim + torque stop and pendulum striker. The shim fixes aperture but exhibits flex and microslip under preload, so preload still changes peak dynamic compression. Current goal: redesign the shim/seating to eliminate flex and slip while keeping impact energy independently variable.
openQuestion: Does increasing shim rigidity and adding a constrained seating flange eliminate flex and microslip under torqueed preload?
